sources.publisher: Sapienza Università di Roma / supplied presidential CV
sources.title: Kaïs Saïed CV: birth, diplomas, teaching and constitutional-law associations
sources.findings: Read the birth, diploma, employment and association sections of the supplied presidential CV hosted by Sapienza’s academic-senate archive. It gives Tunis, 22 February 1958; advanced-studies diploma in public international law 1985; International Academy of Constitutional Law diploma 1986; San Remo humanitarian-law diploma 2001; Sousse teaching 1986–1999 and department leadership 1994–1999; Tunis teaching 1999–2018. Association secretary-general 1990–1995 and vice-president from the 1995 entry are distinct from the separate Tunis constitutional-law-for-democracy centre presidency in 2011. This corrects the raw draft’s association-president claim. Do not invent a doctorate, tenured rank or exact end date for association roles. The CV is supplied biographical material, not independent diploma authentication.

sources.title: 14 October 2019: electoral commission announces 72.71% preliminary runoff result
sources.findings: Read Reuters’ short 14 October 2019 report on Euronews: the electoral commission announced 72.71% for Saied after Sunday’s runoff, and Nabil Karoui conceded. The event was 13 October, not the report date or the 14 October result announcement. These were explicitly preliminary results; the public timeline describes an official reported share without falsely labelling this source final certification. No vote-share inference about all registered voters.

sources.title: 23 October 2019 presidential swearing-in and anticorruption promises
sources.findings: Read Reuters’ 23 October 2019 swearing-in report syndicated by Egypt Independent, including actual inauguration, anticorruption promises and the then-existing division between presidential foreign/defence powers and domestic government leadership. This historical division is not the post-2022 constitutional framework. Promises do not establish completed corruption reduction. The article’s 219 parliamentary-seat statement is not used; no claim to have verified the full legislature from this source.

sources.title: 26 July 2021 account of previous evening’s dismissal and parliamentary suspension
sources.findings: Read relevant Reuters paragraphs on Euronews describing Sunday night 25 July 2021 dismissal of Hichem Mechichi, 30-day parliamentary suspension, constitutional Article 80 justification and opponents’ coup characterization. The 26 July publication date is distinct from the announcement. Dismissal and suspension were later formalized through decrees; the September text references 26 and 29 July instruments. A claim of constitutional authority is not proof of uncontested legality. Suspension is not the March 2022 formal dissolution.

sources.publisher: DCAF Tunisia legal database / presidential decree
sources.title: Presidential Decree 2021-117 of 22 September: selected legislative, executive and constitutional provisions
sources.findings: Read selected French provisions of Decree 2021-117 on the DCAF legal database, with Arabic headings and referenced instruments visible. Articles 1–2 maintain suspension and removal of immunity; Article 4 provides decree-laws after cabinet deliberation and includes rights-protection language; Article 7 precludes annulment appeals against decree-laws; Article 8 vests executive power in the president assisted by government. Article 20 retains the preamble, first two chapters and compatible constitutional provisions; Article 21 removes the provisional constitutional-review body. It is inaccurate to say every constitutional provision was abolished that day or that all possible judicial remedies in every field disappeared. No independent constitutional-validity adjudication or exhaustive bilingual comparison is claimed.

sources.title: 2022–2023 referendum/election final report: selected institutional chronology
sources.findings: Read the Carter Center’s selected institutional timeline and limited introductory passages, not the entire 8291-line report. It separately dates 25 July 2021 suspension, 22 September decree, 30 March 2022 parliamentary dissolution and 25 July 2022 referendum. The chronology corrects the raw draft’s July 2021 dissolution claim. Forecasts, all electoral statistics and unrelated judiciary dates were not imported. This is an observer report, not an official court ruling.

sources.publisher: DCAF Tunisia legal database / Constitution of Tunisia
sources.title: 17 August 2022 promulgation text and selected executive-power provisions
sources.findings: Read the 2022 constitution promulgation preface, Articles 87, 101–102 and 142, and the 17 August signature line on the DCAF database. It distinguishes 25 July referendum, 16 August final electoral decision and 17 August promulgation; no single unsupported precise commencement claim is added where Article 142 links conditions. Presidential appointment and dismissal powers are explicit. The preamble’s celebratory account of July 2021 is the constitutional text’s own political narrative, not a neutral historical verdict. Not every article or original gazette image was reviewed; the database’s duplicated pardon wording at Articles 99–100 is not relied upon.

sources.title: 16 July 2023 partnership announcement: five pillars and actual memorandum signatories
sources.findings: Read the European Commission’s 16 July 2023 announcement: Saied, von der Leyen, Meloni and Rutte witnessed a memorandum actually signed by Olivér Várhelyi and Mounir Ben Rjiba. Five pillars cover macroeconomic stability, trade/investment, green energy, people-to-people contacts and migration. The June 11 package announcement and July signing are separate. Cooperation promises do not demonstrate full payment, reduced irregular migration or rights-compliant implementation; no unverified funding total or personal signature attributed to Saied.

sources.title: October 2024 election: results, turnout and restrictions on competition and observers
sources.findings: Read International IDEA’s October 2024 election and turnout sections: 6 October poll, 90.69% announced share and 28.80% turnout, two opponents, Ayachi Zammel imprisoned, three excluded candidates despite an administrative-court reinstatement ruling, and denied observer accreditation. Preserve restricted competition and opposition boycott context. Its 48.98% 2019 comparison refers to the first round, whereas the runoff had about 55%; public text avoids mixing rounds. Official tallies are not a finding that the process was fully fair.

sources.title: 21 October 2024 inauguration and political-crackdown context
sources.findings: Read AP’s relevant inauguration paragraphs and dated presidency-photo captions. They identify Monday 21 October 2024 swearing-in, amid arrests and restrictions, and report Saied’s justification in anticorruption and state-protection terms. Publication/update on 22 October is not the event date. One body sentence calls it his Oct. 7 re-election; the vote was 6 October and the initial result announcement 7 October, as confirmed by IDEA and indexed TAP. Do not silently propagate the compressed date. AP photos were not visually inspected or licensed for reuse.

sources.title: World Report 2026, events of 2025: political trials and civic-space restrictions
sources.findings: Read Human Rights Watch’s World Report 2026 sections headed Events of 2025, political crackdown and civic-space restrictions, including its concerns about proceedings against political opponents, lawyers and activists and inadequate defence opportunities. These are attributed rights-monitoring assessments, not criminal findings against Saied himself. November and December events in this report refer to 2025, not future 2026 dates. No exact prisoner totals or individual sentence lengths are republished as current in November 2026; the full trial judgments and subsequent appeals were not reviewed.

sources.publisher: Presidency of the Government of Tunisia
sources.title: 17 November 2026 record of Monday’s meeting on public services and development
sources.findings: Read the government portal’s 17 November 2026 account of the Monday meeting with Prime Minister Sarra Zaafrani Zenzri at Carthage, and selected paragraphs on prices, fertilizer distribution, transport, health and delayed development projects. Its title records a completed meeting and the independent outlet dates it 16 November. This establishes recent activity/current presidency, not achieved service improvements. Claims about remnants of the old system or intentional obstruction remain attributed to Saied, not independent findings.

sources.title: 17 November 2026 accessible article opening dates the meeting to 16 November
sources.findings: Read the accessible opening paragraphs of Business News Tunisia’s 17 November 2026 article, explicitly dating the meeting to Monday 16 November and attributing its details to a presidential communiqué. The page displays a subscriber-only label; no subscription-only content or full-body reading is claimed. It corroborates the event date but is not necessarily a separate eyewitness investigation. Reader comments and allegations were not used.
